title: Case 31-2016. A 53-Year-Old Man with Diplopia, Polydipsia, and Polyuria
clinical_vignette: A 53-year-old man presented with a 2-month history of diplopia, progressive thirst (drinking up to 8 liters of water daily), and polyuria. He also reported headaches and fatigue. On examination, he had bilateral sixth cranial nerve palsies. MRI of the brain showed thickening and enhancement of the pituitary stalk and hypothalamus. Laboratory studies revealed diabetes insipidus with low ADH levels. A chest CT showed pulmonary nodules, and there was a history of chronic sinusitis with nasal crusting and saddle nose deformity.

title: Case 22-2016. A 65-Year-Old Man with Syncope
clinical_vignette: A 65-year-old man presented after a syncopal episode. He had a 1-year history of exertional dyspnea and lower extremity edema. Echocardiography showed a thickened left ventricle with a sparkling granular appearance and diastolic dysfunction with preserved ejection fraction. An ECG showed low voltage in the limb leads despite the echocardiographic evidence of ventricular hypertrophy. Serum and urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation showed a monoclonal lambda light chain. A fat pad biopsy showed amorphous deposits that stained positive with Congo red.

title: Too Much of a Good Thing
clinical_vignette: A 45-year-old woman presented with progressive fatigue, bronze discoloration of the skin, arthralgia particularly affecting the second and third metacarpophalangeal joints, and abdominal pain. Laboratory studies revealed markedly elevated serum ferritin (>2000 ng/mL) and transferrin saturation of 85%. Liver function tests were mildly elevated. A liver biopsy showed extensive iron deposition in hepatocytes. Genetic testing was performed.

title: From Dancing to Debilitated
clinical_vignette: A 32-year-old woman who was previously an active dancer presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness over 6 months. She had difficulty climbing stairs and raising her arms above her head. On examination, she had a heliotrope rash on her upper eyelids, Gottron papules over the metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal muscle weakness (4/5). Creatine kinase was markedly elevated at 5,400 U/L. EMG showed myopathic changes. She also reported recent-onset Raynaud phenomenon.

title: A Deficient Diagnosis
clinical_vignette: A 28-year-old man of Ashkenazi Jewish descent presented with progressive splenomegaly, anemia, and thrombocytopenia discovered incidentally. He reported bone pain in the lower extremities and easy bruising. Physical examination revealed hepatosplenomegaly. A bone marrow biopsy showed characteristic crinkled-paper appearing macrophages with accumulated lipid material. Acid phosphatase was elevated. The family history was notable for a sibling with similar symptoms.

title: Diagnostic Challenge: Pheochromocytoma
clinical_vignette: A 38-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a severe hypertensive crisis (blood pressure 240/140 mmHg), palpitations, diaphoresis, and a severe headache. She reported episodic symptoms of anxiety, tremor, and pallor occurring several times per week for the past 3 months, each lasting 15-30 minutes. Between episodes, her blood pressure was normal. A 24-hour urine collection showed markedly elevated catecholamines and metanephrines. Abdominal CT revealed a 4 cm right adrenal mass with heterogeneous enhancement.

title: Diagnostic Challenge: Fabry Disease
clinical_vignette: A 25-year-old man presented with a 10-year history of burning pain in the hands and feet that worsened with exercise and fever. He also reported decreased sweating, recurrent febrile episodes of unknown origin, and corneal changes (cornea verticillata) found on slit-lamp examination. He had small dark red papules (angiokeratomas) clustered in the bathing trunk distribution. Renal function was mildly impaired with proteinuria. Echocardiography showed left ventricular hypertrophy. His maternal uncle had similar symptoms and died of renal failure at age 40.

title: Diagnostic Challenge: Systemic Mastocytosis
clinical_vignette: A 42-year-old woman presented with recurrent episodes of flushing, pruritus, and near-syncope triggered by alcohol, exercise, and emotional stress. She had chronic diarrhea and abdominal cramping. Physical examination revealed numerous small reddish-brown papules on the trunk that urticated on stroking (Darier sign). She had experienced two episodes of unexplained anaphylaxis requiring epinephrine. A bone marrow biopsy showed multifocal dense infiltrates of spindle-shaped mast cells. Serum tryptase was markedly elevated at 85 ng/mL.
key_discriminating_features: mast cell infiltrates in bone marrow

title: Diagnostic Challenge: Sarcoidosis
clinical_vignette: A 35-year-old African American woman presented with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy found on routine chest X-ray, along with erythema nodosum on her shins, bilateral anterior uveitis, and fatigue. She had elevated serum ACE levels and mild hypercalcemia. A transbronchial biopsy showed noncaseating granulomas without evidence of acid-fast bacilli or fungal elements. Pulmonary function tests showed a restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.

title: Diagnostic Challenge: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
clinical_vignette: A 12-year-old boy presented with seizures since age 6, learning difficulties, and a skin examination showing multiple hypomelanotic macules (ash-leaf spots), facial angiofibromas, and a shagreen patch on the lower back. Brain MRI revealed multiple cortical tubers and subependymal nodules, with one subependymal giant cell astrocytoma near the foramen of Monro. Renal ultrasound showed bilateral angiomyolipomas. His mother had similar facial lesions and had been treated for a renal angiomyolipoma.
